title: Quote vs batch Greek assembly mathematical inconsistency in assemble_quote_greeks
expected: assemble_quote_greeks must produce mathematically identical Greeks to _assemble_batch_greeks_gpu, including smile sensitivity chain rule terms (B_Fs + B_ss * s_k * k_F) for Vanna and the calendar theta roll term B_s * s_k * (r_C - r_A).
actual: assemble_quote_greeks used naive Black-76 formulas omitting the smile sensitivity chain rule and omitted the theta roll term entirely, causing single quotes to diverge from batch evaluations by up to 2.24 in theta.
impact: Single quotes served to trading desks have incorrect risk sensitivities and theta carry decays, breaking Greek parity between single-quote and batch endpoints.
recommendation: Include the smile sensitivity chain rule and theta calendar roll term in assemble_quote_greeks to match batch GPU evaluation.

title: Unsynchronized static buffer data race in CPUQuotePath during concurrent CPU fallback
expected: CPUQuotePath must be thread-safe when invoked concurrently by worker threads in _cpu_fallback_pool.
actual: CPUQuotePath maintains instance-level static buffers self._input_buf and self._input_buf_np without mutex synchronization, causing concurrent worker threads to overwrite input features during inference and corrupt pricing outputs by orders of magnitude (78-92% corruption rate).
impact: Concurrent CPU fallback requests yield completely corrupted derivative prices and risk numbers, posing extreme market risk.
recommendation: Protect self._input_buf_np mutation and evaluation in CPUQuotePath.price_single with a thread lock (threading.Lock).

title: FXCrossGPUExecutor cannot be restarted after stop() lifecycle call
expected: Calling start() after stop() must cleanly re-initialize the executor and its background thread pools.
actual: stop() calls self._cpu_fallback_pool.shutdown(), but start() never recreates _cpu_fallback_pool, causing subsequent fallback submissions to raise RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown.
impact: Executor restart during service lifecycle events (e.g. dynamic weights reload or worker pool recycle) leads to unrecoverable service degradation.
recommendation: Recreate self._cpu_fallback_pool in FXCrossGPUExecutor.start() if it is None or shut down.

title: CUDA warmup and graph capture executed directly on asyncio event loop thread
expected: All heavy CUDA warmup and graph capture operations must be offloaded to a worker thread; zero device work on event loop.
actual: reload_fx_cross_weights invokes state['runtime'].warmup_and_capture() directly on the asyncio event loop thread, blocking the event loop for hundreds of milliseconds.
impact: HTTP server event loop is stalled during model reloads, causing severe latency spikes and connection timeouts for incoming HTTP requests.
recommendation: Wrap warmup_and_capture in loop.run_in_executor(None, state['runtime'].warmup_and_capture).

title: Model version remains stale in server state after dynamic weights reload
expected: reload_fx_cross_weights must update _FX_CROSS_STATE['model_version'] to reflect the reloaded weights artifact.
actual: reload_fx_cross_weights updates neural net parameters but leaves state['model_version'] untouched.
impact: Telemetry and health responses continue reporting the pre-reload model version, breaking model provenance and regulatory traceability.
recommendation: Update state['model_version'] using the reloaded weights checkpoint metadata or filename stem.

title: Health endpoint hardcodes status ok and fails to report degraded on CPU fallback
expected: When running on CPU or when CUDA graphs failed to capture, /fx_cross/health must return status degraded.
actual: /fx_cross/health hardcodes status ok regardless of whether the execution backend is CPU or whether CUDA graphs are captured.
impact: Kubernetes / orchestrator health checks cannot detect when GPU acceleration has failed and nodes are degraded.
recommendation: Inspect state['device'] and runtime.graphs_captured; return status degraded if device is CPU or graphs are uncaptured.

title: Corrupted NaN network weights bypass Guardian routing checks and propagate to clients
expected: FXCrossGuardian.route must verify model parameter integrity; if weights contain NaN or Inf, it must trigger emergency analytic fallback.
actual: FXCrossGuardian only inspects input market features against Mahalanobis thresholds. When loaded with corrupted NaN model weights, it sets nn_gate = 1.0 and fallback_activated = False, propagating NaNs directly to market clients.
impact: Model corruption results in invalid NaN quotes served to trading desks without triggering safety fallbacks.
recommendation: Add parameter validation in Guardian to verify that network weights contain zero NaN or Inf values, routing to fallback if detected.

title: Queue depth busy GPU worker blindspot causes single quotes to queue behind saturated GPU
expected: Single quotes must route to CPU fallback whenever the GPU executor is actively executing a task or has queued work.
actual: submit() checks if single and self.queue_depth > 0. When the GPU worker thread is actively executing a batch, the task is already popped, leaving queue_depth == 0. Incoming single quotes see depth 0 and queue behind the busy GPU rather than falling back to CPU.
impact: Single-quote latency spikes under heavy batch workloads, violating the low-latency SLA.
recommendation: Track GPU worker busy state with an active flag; trigger CPU fallback if queue_depth > 0 or worker is actively executing.

title: Single option pricing endpoint catches and swallows SMILE_ARBITRAGE errors with synthetic flat smile
expected: Market smiles failing both SVI and SSVI calibration due to butterfly or calendar arbitrage must be rejected with HTTP 422 SMILE_ARBITRAGE.
actual: _fx_cross_price_impl catches except Exception: on canonicalization failure, synthesizes a flat dummy CanonicalSmile with w_atm, and returns HTTP 200 with fallback pricing.
impact: Severe financial soundness breach: arbitrageable, physically impossible market quotes are quoted and priced rather than rejected, exposing trading desks to severe arbitrage losses.
recommendation: Propagate canonicalization ValueError as HTTP 422 with SMILE_ARBITRAGE detail rather than masking it behind a synthetic flat smile.

title: Insecure torch.load checkpoint deserialization without weights_only=True
expected: All torch.load invocations must explicitly specify weights_only=True to prevent arbitrary Python pickle bytecode execution.
actual: Multiple critical loading paths (model reload in server.py, guardian OOD statistics loading, surrogate member loading) omit weights_only=True.
impact: Remote code execution vulnerability (Bandit B614) via crafted pickle payload injected into model weights or OOD checkpoints.
recommendation: Add weights_only=True to all torch.load calls across server.py, fx_cross_guardian.py, and train_cross_surrogate.py.

title: Runtime crash in reload_fx_cross_weights on official checkpoint dictionary
expected: reload_fx_cross_weights must correctly parse and unpack the official checkpoint dictionary containing state_dict, feature_mean, and feature_std.
actual: reload_fx_cross_weights passes new_state directly to net.load_state_dict, raising RuntimeError: Unexpected key(s): state_dict, feature_mean, feature_std, model_version.
impact: Dynamic weight reloading in production crashes unconditionally on official release checkpoints.
recommendation: Unpack new_state['state_dict'], update engine feature normalization buffers, and update model_version in reload_fx_cross_weights.

title: Omission of Federal Reserve SR 11-7 structured compliance audit logging on fallback and OOD activations
expected: SR 11-7 model governance mandates immutable structured audit logging recording request_id, fallback_reason, and model_version whenever fallback or OOD routing is activated.
actual: Neither server.py nor FXCrossGuardian.route emits structured log events on fallback activations, leaving zero audit trail for regulatory examinations.
impact: Non-compliance with Federal Reserve SR 11-7 model risk management standards; inability to reconstruct fallback triggers during regulatory audits.
recommendation: Add structured logging in Guardian and server.py recording request_id, fallback_reason, and model_version on every fallback activation.

title: FXCrossGuardian MarketStateDriftMonitor is detached from central mrm.compliance framework
expected: MarketStateDriftMonitor must be wired to deepvol.mrm.compliance.DriftMonitor and register 12-D FX cross features into central model governance.
actual: MarketStateDriftMonitor operates as an unlinked class that never reports drift events to compliance._global_monitor, while compliance.py remains hardcoded to 6 Heston parameters.
impact: Central risk compliance dashboards are blind to FX cross feature drift and PSI alerts.
recommendation: Subclass compliance.DriftMonitor in MarketStateDriftMonitor, define FEATURE_NAMES_12D in compliance.py, and connect drift alerting.

title: Model version mismatch between server.py telemetry and official model_card.json
expected: Model version reported by server telemetry must match model_version in model_card.json and committed checkpoints.
actual: server.py hardcodes deepvol-fx-cross-v3.0-b24977e7 while model_card.json and residual_vol_v3_m0.pt record 1326b33ce012+afc6d3f.
impact: Telemetry logs record an untracked, conflicting model version hash, corrupting audit trails.
recommendation: Synchronize server.py default model_version to 1326b33ce012+afc6d3f.

title: Batch pricing endpoint missing HTTP content negotiation (415 on Content-Type and 406 on Accept)
expected: Requests with unsupported Content-Type must return HTTP 415; requests with unsupported Accept must return HTTP 406.
actual: Unsupported Content-Type falls through to JSON decoder and returns 422; unsupported Accept silently defaults to JSON and returns 200 OK.
impact: Contract violation with external trading gateways; clients requesting binary Arrow IPC with invalid Accept headers or sending unexpected MIME types receive unexpected payloads.
recommendation: Validate Content-Type and Accept headers against allowed set and raise HTTP 415 / 406 accordingly.

title: API lacks 50MB request payload size limit exposing endpoint to memory exhaustion DoS
expected: Requests with payload size exceeding 50 MB must be rejected early with HTTP 413 Payload Too Large.
actual: Requests are buffered entirely in memory regardless of size and only fail later during deserialization with 422 Unprocessable Entity.
impact: OOM crash risk and memory exhaustion denial-of-service vector under high-concurrency or malicious oversized streaming uploads.
recommendation: Enforce 50MB payload limit check on Content-Length header and request body, raising HTTP 413 if exceeded.

title: Developer test suite loosened Gate G2.6 heartbeat jitter batch size and latency SLA
expected: WebSocket heartbeat jitter p99 must be strictly < 2.0 ms during a full 10,000-contract batch pricing workload.
actual: Developer test suite reduced workload to 1,000 contracts and loosened assertion to < 3.0 ms; even under loosened threshold, measured 3.851 ms in concurrent audit runs.
impact: Masks SLA breach under true 10k institutional batch load.
recommendation: Restore test suite to 10k contracts and enforce strict < 2.0 ms jitter threshold.

title: Missing artifacts/reports/spec_deviations.md due to .gitignore whitelist omission
expected: artifacts/reports/spec_deviations.md must be committed to repository under delivery requirements.
actual: .gitignore ignores artifacts/reports/* except a whitelist of 4 files (fx_cross_gates.json, fx_cross_progress.md, wolfram_proofs.md, model_card.json), inadvertently excluding spec_deviations.md.
impact: Documentation delivery gap; deviation tracking is absent from git version control.
recommendation: Add !artifacts/reports/spec_deviations.md to .gitignore whitelist and commit the document.

title: Zero-tolerance modules coverage shortfall (< 100% line and branch coverage)
expected: 100% line and 100% branch coverage across all three zero-tolerance modules.
actual: Pre-remediation coverage shortfalls identified in coverage_report.md.
impact: Uncovered branches in safeguards, schemas, and guardian.
recommendation: Implement exhaustive test suite covering all remaining branches.

title: PyTorch autograd detect_anomaly state leakage across test cases
expected: Anomaly detection enabled only within isolated context managers or cleaned up in finally blocks.
actual: Global set_detect_anomaly(True) leaked across tests, adding runtime overhead and side-effects.
impact: Test suite state leakage and performance degradation.
recommendation: Wrap anomaly detection calls in context managers and restore prior state.

title: Missing boundary condition assertions for extreme market states
expected: Strict assertion of boundaries and zero-tolerance paths.
actual: Edge case testing expanded to cover full zero-tolerance surface.
impact: Incomplete boundary verification.
recommendation: Add comprehensive boundary parameter fixtures and property tests.

title: Cross-engine Greek parity oracle tests
expected: Exact mathematical oracle assertions across all Greek sensitivities.
actual: Parity verified against closed-form Garman-Kohlhagen and copula oracles.
impact: Assurance of Greek fidelity across pricing backends.
recommendation: Implement independent clean-room mathematical oracles in test suite.

title: Tautological isfinite() assertions masking numerical calculation errors
expected: Strict assertion against closed-form numerical oracles; rejection of tautological assert isfinite().
actual: Test cases asserted merely torch.isfinite() without validating numerical values or sign correctness.
impact: Defects in sensitivity calculations went undetected because tests passed as long as output was finite.
recommendation: Replace tautological assertions with exact analytical oracles and symmetry invariants.
